chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayoub, from Sa'd al-Askaf, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the pilgrim begins his preparation, he does not take a step with regards to something from his preparations, except that Allah Mighty and Majestic Writes ten good deeds for him, and Deletes ten sins from him, and Raises ten Levels for him, until he is free from his preparations. When he is free and he faces his ride with it, he does not place a shoe nor does he raise it, except that Allah Mighty and Majestic Writes for him similar to that until he has completed his rituals. So when he has completed his rituals, Allah Forgives his sins for him.'

And Dhu al-Hijjah, and Al-Muharram, and Safar, and the month of Rabi' al-Awwal are four months in which the good deeds are Written for him and the sins are not Written against him, except if he comes to a major sin. So when the four months are past, he is mixed with the people'.

key_terms.خُلِطَ بِالنَّاس: Mixed with the people (returning to normal state)
key_terms.مُوجِبَة: Major sin / Cause for recording sins

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards and sins forgiveness for a Muslim during the Hajj preparation and journey?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the cumulative spiritual merit of Hajj, emphasizing that the intention and preparation phase are as significant as the rituals themselves, with rewards accruing for every step. It introduces the concept of 'Istiqra' (residence) in the sacred months, where a pilgrim who remains in a state of ritual purity and devotion enjoys a unique period where good deeds are recorded but minor sins are not, a state that ends upon rejoining the general populace. This underscores the Shia scholarly view of Hajj as a comprehensive spiritual journey beginning with the heart's intention and physical preparation.
